extracted.intended_audience: patent proprietors, alleged infringers, patent attorneys, national courts and judges, and other users of the Unified Patent Court system
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural, substantive and organisational rules governing infringement, revocation, remedies, appeals, enforcement and the appointment and conduct of judges under the Agreement on a Unified Patent Court and its Statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a decision is taken finding an infringement of a patent, the Court may grant an injunction against the infringer aimed at prohibiting the continuation of the infringement. The Court may also grant such injunction against an intermediary whose services are being used by a third party to infringe a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance with the injunction may be subject to a recurring penalty payment payable to the Court (where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective measures available in infringement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may order, at the request of the applicant, appropriate measures with regard to products found to be infringing a patent and, in appropriate cases, with regard to materials and implements principally used in the creation or manufacture of those products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures include declaration of infringement; recalling products from channels of commerce; depriving the product of its infringing property; definitively removing products from commerce; destruction of products and/or materials and implements concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of corrective measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Those corrective measures shall be carried out at the expense of the infringer, unless particular reasons are invoked for not doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court must consider any invoked particular reasons before ordering that infringer bear costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionality in ordering remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering a request for corrective measures the Court shall take into account the need for proportionality between the seriousness of the infringement and the remedies to be ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court shall also consider the willingness of the infringer to convert materials into non-infringing state and the interests of third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on validity (revocation) basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall decide on the validity of a patent on the basis of an action for revocation or a counterclaim for revocation and may revoke a patent, either entirely or partly, only on the grounds referred to in Articles 138(1) and 139(2) of the EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation must conform to EPC-specified grounds; the Court's revocation powers are limited to those grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial revocation and limitation of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the grounds for revocation affect the patent only in part, the patent shall be limited by a corresponding amendment of the claims and revoked in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limiting patent via claim amendment where revocation grounds are partial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of revocation (retroactivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent that a patent has been revoked it shall be deemed not to have had, from the outset, the effects specified in Articles 64 and 67 of the EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation may have retroactive effect for the specified EPC effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of revocation decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Court, in a final decision, revokes a patent, either entirely or partly, it shall send a copy of the decision to the European Patent Office and, with respect to a European patent, to the national patent office of any Contracting Member State concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures administrative bodies are notified of revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's powers concerning EPO decisions in certain actions
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions brought under Article 32(1)(i), the Court may exercise any power entrusted on the European Patent Office in accordance with Article 9 of Regulation (EU) No 1257/2012, including the rectification of the Register for unitary patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For such actions the Court steps into certain EPO powers to deal with unitary patent register matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs rule for actions exercising EPO powers
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions brought under Article 32(1)(i) the parties shall, by way of derogation from Article 69, bear their own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties cannot rely on general cost-shifting in these specific actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to order communication of information from infringer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may order an infringer to inform the applicant of the origin and distribution channels of the infringing products or processes; the quantities produced, manufactured, delivered, received or ordered, and the price obtained; and the identity of any third person involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order available in response to a justified and proportionate request of the applicant and in accordance with the Rules of Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to order third parties to provide information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may order third parties who (a) were found in possession of infringing products on a commercial scale, (b) were providing services used in infringing activities on a commercial scale, or (c) were indicated as involved in production/distribution, to provide the applicant with the information referred to in paragraph 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application governed by the Rules of Procedure; targets commercial-scale third-party involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for awarding damages (knowledge threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall order the infringer who knowingly, or with reasonable grounds to know, engaged in a patent infringing activity, to pay the injured party damages appropriate to the harm actually suffered by that party as a result of the infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge or reasonable grounds to know is the threshold for ordering damages for harm actually suffered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of damages (compensatory, not punitive)
rubrics_metrics.description: The injured party shall, to the extent possible, be placed in the position it would have been in if no infringement had taken place. The infringer shall not benefit from the infringement. However, damages shall not be punitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damages aim to compensate and remove unjust enrichment but are not punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for setting damages
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Court sets the damages it shall take into account appropriate aspects such as negative economic consequences (including lost profits), any unfair profits made by the infringer and, in appropriate cases, elements other than economic factors, such as moral prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may weigh multiple economic and non-economic elements when calculating damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative lump-sum damages method
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative, the Court may, in appropriate cases, set the damages as a lump sum on the basis of elements such as at least the amount of the royalties or fees which would have been due if the infringer had requested authorisation to use the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lump-sum approach may be used where appropriate instead of itemised compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies where infringer lacked knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the infringer did not knowingly, or with reasonable grounds to know, engage in the infringing activity, the Court may order the recovery of profits or the payment of compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less culpable infringers may face disgorgement or compensation rather than full damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of legal costs (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable and proportionate legal costs and other expenses incurred by the successful party shall, as a general rule, be borne by the unsuccessful party, unless equity requires otherwise, up to a ceiling set in accordance with the Rules of Procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a cap (ceiling) on recoverable costs established in the Rules of Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment of costs in partial success or exceptional circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a party succeeds only in part or in exceptional circumstances, the Court may order that costs be apportioned equitably or that the parties bear their own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court has discretion to apportion costs when outcomes are mixed or exceptional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction for causing unnecessary costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A party should bear any unnecessary costs it has caused the Court or another party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are responsible for costs resulting from their unnecessary conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security for legal costs on defendant request
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the defendant, the Court may order the applicant to provide adequate security for the legal costs and other expenses incurred by the defendant which the applicant may be liable to bear, in particular in the cases referred to in Articles 59 to 62.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendants may request cost security where appropriate; applies especially in certain expedited/urgent procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court fees payment obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties to proceedings before the Court shall pay court fees. Court fees shall be paid in advance, unless the Rules of Procedure provide otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any party which has not paid a prescribed court fee may be excluded from further participation in the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal aid availability and decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who is a natural person and who is unable to meet the costs of the proceedings may at any time apply for legal aid. The conditions for granting legal aid shall be laid down in the Rules of Procedure. The Court shall decide whether legal aid should be granted in full or in part, or whether it should be refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Committee proposes level and rules for legal aid and bearing of costs on proposal from the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation period for financial compensation actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions relating to all forms of financial compensation may not be brought more than five years after the date on which the applicant became aware, or had reasonable grounds to become aware, of the last fact justifying the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five-year limitation applies subject to Article 24(2) and (3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal time limits (general and specific orders)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal against a decision of the Court of First Instance may be brought within two months of the date of the notification of the decision. An appeal against certain orders (Articles 49(5), 59 to 62 and 67) must be brought within 15 calendar days of notification; other orders within 15 days either together with the appeal against the decision or where leave is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different time limits apply for decisions vs specific interlocutory orders; parties must follow the specified deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for appeal and new evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal may be based on points of law and matters of fact. New facts and new evidence may only be introduced in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and where submission thereof could not reasonably have been expected during proceedings before the Court of First Instance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules restrict the introduction of new evidence to exceptional situations to preserve finality and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspensive effect of appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal shall not have suspensive effect unless the Court of Appeal decides otherwise. Notwithstanding this, an appeal against a decision on actions or counterclaims for revocation and on actions based on Article 32(1)(i) shall always have suspensive effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particular categories of appeals (revocation-related and certain Article 32 actions) automatically suspend enforcement; others require express decision by Court of Appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of appeals on continuation of main proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal against an order referred to in Articles 49(5), 59 to 62 or 67 shall not prevent the continuation of the main proceedings. However, the Court of First Instance shall not give a decision in the main proceedings before the decision of the Court of Appeal concerning an appealed order has been given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlocutory appeals do not necessarily halt main proceedings but may prevent final decisions until resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on appeal and referral back
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appeal is well-founded, the Court of Appeal shall revoke the decision of the Court of First Instance and give a final decision. The Court of Appeal may in exceptional cases refer the case back to the Court of First Instance for decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where referred back, the Court of First Instance is bound by the Court of Appeal's decision on points of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of what the Court may award
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall decide in accordance with the requests submitted by the parties and shall not award more than is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties shape the scope of relief; court cannot exceed claimed relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions based only on submitted grounds/facts/evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on the merits may only be based on grounds, facts and evidence which were submitted by the parties or introduced into the procedure by an order of the Court and on which the parties have had an opportunity to present their comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures parties' right to be heard and to comment on evidence relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free and independent evaluation of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall evaluate evidence freely and independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No predetermined evidentiary hierarchy; judges assess probative value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions and orders of the Court shall be reasoned and shall be given in writing in accordance with the Rules of Procedure. Decisions and orders shall be delivered in the language of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires reasoned, written decisions and adherence to proceeding language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making and dissenting opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions and orders of the Court shall be taken by a majority of the panel; in case of equal votes, the vote of the presiding judge shall prevail. In exceptional circumstances, any judge may express a dissenting opinion separately from the decision of the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides for majority rule, casting vote of presiding judge and limited right to dissent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement confirmation and limitation on settlement effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may conclude their case by way of settlement, which shall be confirmed by a decision of the Court. A patent may not be revoked or limited by way of settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement can end proceedings but cannot be used to revoke or limit a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and dissemination of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may order, at the request of the applicant and at the expense of the infringer, appropriate measures for the dissemination of information concerning the Court's decision, including displaying the decision and publishing it in full or in part in public media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication can be ordered as corrective/public interest remedy, costs borne by infringer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and time limits for rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rehearing after a final decision may exceptionally be granted on discovery of a decisive fact unknown at the time (subject to criminal-offence nexus) or in the event of a fundamental procedural defect (in particular lack of timely service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be filed within 10 years of the date of the decision but not later than two months from discovery of the new fact or procedural defect; rehearing generally does not have suspensive effect unless Court of Appeal decides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of good faith users on rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons using patents which are the subject-matter of a decision under review and who act in good faith should be allowed to continue using such patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearing remedies should protect third parties who relied in good faith on the original decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability of Court decisions across Contracting States
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions and orders of the Court shall be enforceable in any Contracting Member State. An order for the enforcement of a decision shall be appended to the decision by the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures cross-border enforceability; enforcement procedures are governed by national law where enforcement takes place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of security for enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, the enforcement of a decision may be subject to the provision of security or an equivalent assurance to ensure compensation for any damage suffered, in particular in the case of injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security may be required to protect against wrongful enforcement damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for non-compliance with orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party does not comply with the terms of an order of the Court, that party may be sanctioned with a recurring penalty payment payable to the Court. The individual penalty shall be proportionate to the importance of the order to be enforced and shall be without prejudice to the party's right to claim damages or security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions are proportionate and do not preclude separate damage claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional regime for national court competence
rubrics_metrics.description: During a transitional period of seven years after entry into force, an action for infringement or for revocation of a European patent (or for a SPC) may still be brought before national courts or other competent national authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pending national actions at the end of the transitional period are not affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-out and withdrawal procedure during transitional period
rubrics_metrics.description: Proprietors/applicants of European patents (granted or applied for prior to the end of the transitional period) and holders of SPCs may opt out from the exclusive competence of the Court by notifying their opt-out to the Registry at the latest one month before expiry of the transitional period. Opt-out takes effect upon entry in the register. Withdrawals of opt-outs are permitted at any moment and take effect upon entry in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opt-out only if action not already brought before a national court; withdrawal gives ability to re-enter UPC competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and possible extension of transitional period
rubrics_metrics.description: Five years after entry into force, the Administrative Committee shall carry out a broad consultation and a survey on cases still brought before national courts and may, based on consultation and Court opinion, decide to prolong the transitional period by up to seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension depends on user consultation and Court opinion; Administrative Committee action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who is a national of a Contracting Member State and fulfils the conditions set out in Article 15 of the Agreement and in this Statute may be appointed as a judge. Judges shall have a good command of at least one official language of the European Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience with patent litigation required for appointment may be acquired by training under the Statute's training provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment procedure for judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges shall be appointed pursuant to the procedure set out in Article 16 of the Agreement. Vacancies shall be publicly advertised and indicate relevant eligibility criteria. The Advisory Committee shall give an opinion comprising a list of most suitable candidates with at least twice as many candidates as vacancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory Committee may recommend training prior to appointment; appointment decisions shall ensure legal and technical expertise and balanced geographic composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment details to specify instance and technology fields
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the Administrative Committee appointing full-time or part-time legally qualified judges and full-time technically qualified judges shall state the instance of the Court and/or the division of the Court of First Instance for which each judge is appointed and the field(s) of technology for which a technically qualified judge is appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part-time technically qualified judges be included in the Pool of Judges based on specific qualifications to ensure coverage of all fields of technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' term of office
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges shall be appointed for a term of six years, beginning on the date laid down in the instrument of appointment. They may be re-appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default term commencement rules apply where date not specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee member appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Member State shall propose a member of the Advisory Committee who fulfils the requirements set out in Article 14(2) of the Agreement. Members shall be appointed by the Administrative Committee acting by common accord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National proposals and Administrative Committee appointment by consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' oath and duties of confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Before taking up their duties judges shall, in open court, take an oath to perform their duties impartially and conscientiously and to preserve the secrecy of the deliberations of the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath is given publicly and covers impartiality, conscientiousness and secrecy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and grounds for recusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges shall sign a declaration undertaking to respect obligations including integrity and discretion. Judges may not take part in proceedings where they have acted as adviser, been a party or acted for a party, previously pronounced in the matter, have a personal or financial interest, or are related to a party or representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a judge considers they should not take part they must inform the President; any party may object to a judge on listed grounds; difficulties are settled by the Presidium in accordance with the Rules of Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immunity of judges and waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges shall be immune from legal proceedings for acts performed in relation to their official capacity; immunity may be waived by the Presidium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where immunity is waived and criminal proceedings are instituted, the judge shall be tried only by the court competent to judge members of the highest national judiciary; Protocol on privileges and immunities applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: End of duties, resignation and vacancy filling
rubrics_metrics.description: Duties of a judge end on resignation, replacement after term expiry, death or other cases. Resignation letter addressed to the President; judge continues until successor takes up duties; vacancies filled by appointment for remainder of term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural steps for communication and continuity ensure no gap in duties whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal from office procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge may be deprived of office or benefits only if the Presidium decides that the judge no longer fulfils requisite conditions or obligations. The judge concerned shall be heard but shall not take part in deliberations. The Registrar communicates the decision to the Chairman of the Administrative Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal process includes hearing and written communication; vacancy arises upon notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training framework for judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate and regular training of judges shall be provided within the training framework set up under Article 19 of the Agreement. Training Regulations will ensure implementation and coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framework shall organise courses, conferences, seminars, workshops; cooperate with international organisations and education institutes; promote vocational training; include an annual work programme and individual annual training plans for each judge; ensure training for candidate-judges and newly appointed judges and support projects facilitating cooperation between representatives, patent attorneys and the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration setting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Committee shall set the remuneration of the President of the Court of Appeal, the President of the Court of First Instance, the judges, the Registrar, the Deputy-Registrar and the staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Committee responsible for pay scales and related decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election and duties of the President of the Court of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the Court of Appeal shall be elected by all judges of the Court of Appeal for a term of three years, may be re-elected twice, elected by secret ballot requiring absolute majority (or most votes in second ballot). The President directs judicial activities and administration and chairs the Court of Appeal sitting as a full Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vacancy mid-term filled by election for remainder; election procedures set out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election and duties of the President of the Court of First Instance
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the Court of First Instance shall be elected by all full-time judges of the Court of First Instance for a three-year term, may be re-elected twice; the first President shall be a national of the Contracting Member State hosting the seat of the central division. The President directs judicial activities and administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 13(2) and (4) rules apply by analogy (secret ballot, majority, vacancy rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and responsibilities of the Presidium
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presidium shall be composed of specified members (President of the Court of Appeal as chairperson, President of the Court of First Instance, two judges of the Court of Appeal, three full-time judges of the Court of First Instance, and the Registrar as a non-voting member). The Presidium shall exercise duties in accordance with the Statute and is responsible for management of the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include proposing Rules of Procedure and Financial Regulations, preparing budget and annual report, establishing training guidelines, appointing/removing Registrar, laying down Registry rules and giving opinions; decisions in Articles 7, 8, 10 and 22 taken without Registrar; Presidium decisions valid only with all members present or duly represented and by majority vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff role
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials and other servants of the Court shall have the task of assisting the President of the Court of Appeal, the President of the Court of First Instance, the judges and the Registrar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff support judicial and registry functions as delegated by the Presidium and Administrative Committee.
